key_insight: This paper shows that in modern mixture-of-experts models, shared experts and fine-grained expert splitting can unintentionally work against each other: shared experts reduce how much the router explores different expert choices. The core takeaway is that routing quality depends not just on capacity, but on preserving exploration during training.
problem_solved: It addresses the routing exploration problem in modern MoE architectures, where adding shared experts can make the router overly conservative and reduce effective use of the expert pool. The paper asks how to maintain diverse expert assignment while still benefiting from shared and fine-grained experts.
method: Analyzes the interaction between fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts in MoE routing.
Identifies the exploration dilemma: shared experts can dominate token assignments and suppress router diversity.
Proposes a routing perspective that rebalances exploration so the router continues to evaluate more expert combinations during training.
impact: This matters because MoE performance depends heavily on how well tokens are distributed across experts. Better routing exploration can improve expert utilization, model capacity efficiency, and overall accuracy without changing the core MoE scale-up strategy.

paper_title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Bingcong Li, Hao Ma, Michael Muehlebach, Niao He, Yi Ma
